articles.title: eMudhra quit the CA business today. I checked your trust store — its roots are still in it.
articles.excerpt: Two days ago I wrote up the eMudhra incident: eight of the CA's intermediate private keys turned out to be integers smaller than 256 — I recovered all eight in 11 milliseconds, the largest was 237. To…
articles.body: Two days ago I wrote up the eMudhra incident: eight of the CA's intermediate private keys turned out to be integers smaller than 256 — I recovered all eight in 11 milliseconds, the largest was 237. Today eMudhra announced it is leaving the global SSL/TLS certificate business entirely (press release, Bengaluru, October 22; 894 points on Hacker News). A CA whose keys fit in a uint8 has decided certificates aren't worth it. Fair enough. But "a CA exits the business" is a press-release sentence, not a technical event — so I checked the three places where an exit would actually have to happen: your trust store, Mozilla's revocation list, and the incident record.
articles.author: frank chu

articles.title: I built OpenShell's Z3 policy prover and ran 29 checks. It caught everything except the metadata address.
articles.excerpt: OpenShell — NVIDIA's "safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents" — hit the Hacker News front page today (257 points; the repo is at 17,719 stars, v0.1.5 shipped October 20). Most agent…
articles.body: OpenShell — NVIDIA's "safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents" — hit the Hacker News front page today (257 points; the repo is at 17,719 stars, v0.1.5 shipped October 20). Most agent sandboxes sell you enforcement: Landlock, seccomp, a network proxy. OpenShell sells those too, but its headline differentiator is the second half: formal verification . Before a policy change is applied, an SMT-based prover checks what the change would allow. That prover ships as a standalone CLI, openshell-prover , whose job is a boundary check: given a candidate policy and a boundary policy (the most access an environment allows), decide whether the candidate stays inside the boundary — and if not, produce a counterexample.

articles.title: A 3-State Cheap Large File Browser Multipart Upload Retention Ledger with Presigned Parts
articles.excerpt: TL;DR: Reproducible deletion changes the upload decision. For large training artifacts sent from a browser, use presigned multipart uploads when you can own a three-state record in your database: uplo…
articles.body: TL;DR: Reproducible deletion changes the upload decision. For large training artifacts sent from a browser, use presigned multipart uploads when you can own a three-state record in your database: uploading , retained , and deletion_due . Keep the bytes off the Node.js control plane, require every multipart session to complete or abort, and make retention a property of the application record rather than a promise inferred from the bucket. Choose tus or UploadThing when polished interruption recovery matters more than a small storage contract; choose AWS S3 when versioning, Object Lock, or deeper native governance is mandatory. The useful invariant is blunt: an artifact is not retained because its parts exist, and it is not deleted because a database row disappeared.

articles.title: Europe's Space Rider vehicle comes crashing down during drop test
articles.excerpt: The full-scale prototype of Europe's Space Rider orbiter failed to deploy its parachute during a drop test earlier this month, but ESA officials hope the setback won't delay progress toward its first…
articles.body: Europe has dropped the ball on the prototype for its first reusable spacecraft. Or, rather, the prototype itself was dropped — on purpose — but the outcome of its fall was not what engineers had hoped for. The incident occurred during an Oct. 6 drop test of the full-scale Space Rider model , from the European Space Agency (ESA). The robotic vehicle's initial drogue parachute deployed successfully, but its main parafoil detached during deployment, leaving the prototype unable to slow its descent before crashing into the ground, according to ESA officials. The cause of the failure remains under investigation.

articles.excerpt: This NASA Hubble Space Telescope image released on Oct. 16, 2026, features the edge-on, intermediate spiral galaxy NGC 1827, located roughly 37 million light-years away in the constellation Columba, t…
articles.body: NASA, ESA, Michael Jones (California Institute of Technology); Image Processing: Gladys Kober (NASA/Catholic University of America) This NASA Hubble Space Telescope image released on Oct. 16, 2026, features the edge-on, intermediate spiral galaxy NGC 1827, located roughly 37 million light-years away in the constellation Columba, the Dove. Hubble captured the image as part of a survey looking at 260 satellite galaxies around 22 Milky Way-like host galaxies within a radius of about 32 million light-years from Earth. Low-mass galaxies like the ones in this Hubble observing program provide a way to test the predictions of cosmological models on small scales, which struggle to match observations.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 22, 1992: Ashes of 'Star Trek' creator Gene Roddenberry launch into space on NASA shuttle
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 22, 1992, the space shuttle Columbia launched into space with the ashes of Gene Roddenberry, the creator of "Star Trek." Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 22, 1992, the space shuttle Columbia launched into space with the ashes of Gene Roddenberry, the creator of " Star Trek ," aboard. During mission STS-52, NASA astronaut and shuttle commander James Wetherbee brought a small container with a portion of Roddenberry's ashes into space as part of his personal effects at the request of Roddenberry's widow, Majel Barrett . It was Roddenberry's lifelong dream to go to space, but he never got to go while he was alive. But thanks to his wife, a little bit of Roddenberry finally made it to space almost exactly one year after his death. NASA and his family didn't tell anyone about it until almost two years later in 1994. Wetherbee said he was "honored to be asked" by Barrett to carry Roddenberry's ashses on the spaceflight.

articles.title: The 2027 total solar eclipse will plunge these 10 ancient Egyptian temples and monuments into darkness
articles.excerpt: The "eclipse of the century" will plunge some of ancient Egypt's most spectacular sites into darkness on Aug. 2, 2027. These temples, tombs and monuments are inside the path of totality.
articles.body: The total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027, has an ancient feel. It will certainly be a celestial event for the ages — at 6 minutes 23 seconds, it will feature the longest totality on land of the 21st century and the longest anywhere until 2114. However, its point of greatest eclipse occurs just a few miles from Thebes, the magnificent religious and political capital of ancient Egypt's Middle Kingdom and New Kingdom. On the east bank of the mighty Nile is Luxor, the great city of the living, with its massive temple complexes of Karnak and Luxor. On its west bank is the city of the dead, which includes the Valley of the Kings and the Temple of Hatshepsut. articles.body: Tesla says it’s building its own maps to fix some of the most common problems with its “Full Self-Driving” system, including reading speed limits, parking, and choosing routes. The company’s head of AI described the effort on Tesla’s Q3 2026 earnings call. It’s a notable shift for a company whose CEO spent years arguing that self-driving systems relying on maps are brittle. And it shows Tesla’s fleet is now doing the same job Waymo’s cars do: mapping the roads so the self-driving system knows what it can’t reliably figure out on its own.
